predecessors.name: Gupta Empire
predecessors.text: Saurashtra and Gujarat: Bhatarka was 'a military governor of Saurashtra under Gupta Empire' and 'had established himself as the independent around 475 CE'

successors.name: Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty
successors.text: Gujarat and Saurashtra, where Cliopatria's Gurjara-Pratihara shape of 776 covers 603 of the 637 cells of the Maitraka core

successors.name: Rashtrakuta dynasty
successors.text: the Surat and Bharuch edge of southern Gujarat (32 cells)

ledger.x: 475: Bhatarka makes himself independent in Saurashtra.
476: the rest of Gujarat joins the new Maitraka state.
555: the south-east of the Maitraka shape grows.
555: the rest of the added edge belongs to no Cliopatria state.

c. 640: the Maitrakas come under Harsha. 'They came under the rule of Harṣa of Vardhana dynasty in the mid-seventh century' but 'retained local autonomy'; Dhruvasena II 'married the daughter of Harṣavardhana'. The page gives only 'mid-seventh century', so 640, Dhruvasena II's accession on the Vallabhi list (640-644)…
647: the Maitrakas regain their independence on Harsha's death.
723: the Arab governor of Sindh, Junayd, raids Gujarat.
736: a Gurjara king of southern Gujarat is a vassal of Vallabhi.
776: the Maitraka line ends and with it the suzerainty over Nandipuri.
776: the Maitraka kingdom ends at Vallabhi.

wars.name: Arab campaigns in Gujarat (Junayd and al-Hakam)
wars.outcome: Junayd (723-726) 'conquered Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan' but 'forces invaded Malwa and achieved victory' while Ujjain was not taken; his gains were lost under Tamim (726); al-Hakam (731-740) campaigned into Gujarat, overran Nandipuri (736) and was defeated…

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for the Maitrakas; the shape is an approximate Gujarat and Saurashtra block with Ujjain from 616.
